sentences.zh: 河東道，蓋古冀州之域，漢河東、太原、上黨、西河、鴈門、代郡及鉅鹿、常山、趙國、廣平國之地。

translations.literal: The Hedong Circuit — broadly the territory of ancient Jizhou, comprising the Han commanderies of Hedong, Taiyuan, Shangdang, Xihe, Yanmen, and Dai and the principalities of Julu, Changshan, Zhao, and Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: The Hedong Circuit lay within the ancient Jizhou region, covering the Han commanderies of Hedong, Taiyuan, Shangdang, Xihe, Yanmen, and Dai together with the principalities of Julu, Changshan, Zhao, and Guangping.

sentences.zh: 河中、絳、晉、慈、隰、石、太原、汾、忻、潞、澤、沁、遼為實沈分，代、雲、朔、蔚、武、新、嵐、憲為大梁分。

translations.literal: Hezhong, Jiang, Jin, Ci, Xi, Shi, Taiyuan, Fen, Xin, Lu, Ze, Qin, and Liao were the Shen division; Dai, Yun, Shuo, Wei, Wu, Xin, Lan, and Xian were the Daliang division.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhong, Jiang, Jin, Ci, Xi, Shi, Taiyuan, Fen, Xin, Lu, Ze, Qin, and Liao fell within the Shen asterism division; Dai, Yun, Shuo, Wei, Wu, Xin, Lan, and Xian within the Daliang division.

sentences.zh: 為府二，州十九，縣百一十。

translations.literal: It had two superior prefectures, nineteen prefectures, and one hundred ten counties.
translations.idiomatic: The circuit comprised two superior prefectures, nineteen prefectures, and one hundred ten counties.

translations.literal: Its famous mountains: Leishou, Jie, Huo, and Wutai.
translations.idiomatic: Its notable mountains were Leishou, Jie, Huo, and Wutai.

translations.literal: Its great rivers: Fen, Qin, Dan, and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Its major rivers were the Fen, Qin, Dan, and Lu.

translations.literal: Its levied tribute: cloth and fine ramie.
translations.idiomatic: Its assessed tribute consisted of cloth and fine ramie textiles.

sentences.zh: 厥貢：布、席、豹尾、熊鞹、鵰羽。

translations.literal: Its presented tribute: cloth, mats, leopard tails, bear hides, and hawk feathers.
translations.idiomatic: Its presented tribute included cloth, mats, leopard tails, bear hides, and hawk feathers.

translations.literal: Hezhong Superior Prefecture, Hezhong Superior Prefecture, Hedong Commandery, chief.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhong Superior Prefecture (Hedong Commandery designation), chief seat.

translations.literal: Originally Puzhou; an upper auxiliary seat.
translations.idiomatic: It was formerly Puzhou, ranked as an upper auxiliary prefecture.

sentences.zh: 義寧元年治桑泉，武德三年徙治河東。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yining the seat was at Sangquan; in the third year of Wude it was moved to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yining the administration was at Sangquan; in the third year of Wude it was relocated to Hedong.

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kaiyuan the Central Capital was established as a superior prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Kaiyuan the Central Capital was established and made a superior prefecture;

translations.literal: that same year the capital status was abolished and it reverted to a prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: that same year the capital was abolished and it again became a prefecture.

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianyuan it was again made a superior prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Qianyuan it was restored as a superior prefecture.

sentences.zh: 土貢：氈、𪌭扇、龍骨、棗、鳳棲梨。

translations.literal: Local tribute: felt, woven fans, dragon bones, jujubes, and Fengqi pears.
translations.idiomatic: Its local tribute products were felt, woven fans, dragon bones, jujubes, and Fengqi pears.

sentences.zh: 戶七萬八百，口四十六萬九千二百一十三。

translations.literal: Households: 70,800; persons: 469,213.
translations.idiomatic: It had 70,800 households and a population of 469,213.

translations.literal: Thirteen counties.
translations.idiomatic: It administered thirteen counties.

sentences.zh: 有府十八，曰興政、復化、寧靜、洞渦、五泉、昌寧、志節、汾陽、靜智、信童、晉原、聞陽、清定、豐川、竹馬、攘胡、西胡、文谷。城中有天兵軍，開元十一年廢。

translations.literal: It had eighteen military establishments, called Xingzheng, Fuhua, Ningjing, Dongwo, Wuquan, Changning, Zhijie, Fenyang, Jingzhi, Xintong, Jinyuan, Wenyang, Qingding, Fengchuan, Zhumi, Ranghu, Xihu, and Wengu. Within the city it had Tianbing Army, abolished in Kaiyuan year eleven.
translations.idiomatic: It had eighteen military establishments, called Xingzheng, Fuhua, Ningjing, Dongwo, Wuquan, Changning, Zhijie, Fenyang, Jingzhi, Xintong, Jinyuan, Wenyang, Qingding, Fengchuan, Zhumi, Ranghu, Xihu, and Wengu. Within the city it had Tianbing Army, abolished in Kaiyuan year eleven.

sentences.zh: 有府三十三，曰興樂、德義、胡壁、龍亭、清源、永和、陶城、霍山、瀵水、首陽、壽貴、歸仁、長渠、虞城、通閏、寶鼎、鹽海、歸淳、大陽、永安、奉信、永興、右威、汾陰、甘泉、平川、安保、石門、綏化、壇道、安邑、崇義、六軍。又有耀德軍，乾元二年置，廣德二年廢。河東，次赤。有芳醞監、汲河以釀，武德三年置，貞觀十年廢。南有風陵關，聖曆元年置。有歷山。河西，次赤。開元八年析河東置，尋省。乾元三年更同州之朝邑曰河西，來屬。大曆五年復還同州，析朝邑、河東別置。有蒲津關，一名蒲坂。開元十二年鑄八牛，牛有一人策之，牛下有山，皆鐵也，夾岸以維浮梁。十五年自朝邑徙河瀆祠于此。臨晉，次畿。本桑泉，武德三年析置溫泉縣，九年省。天寶十三載更名。解，次畿。本虞鄉，武德元年更名。貞觀十七年省，以地入虞鄉，二十二年復置。有鹽池，又有女鹽池。有紫泉監，乾元元年置，有銅穴十二。猗氏，次畿，有孤山。虞鄉，次畿。武德元年別置。貞觀二十二年省，以地入解。天授二年復置。北十五里有涑水渠，貞觀十七年，刺史薛萬徹開，自聞喜引涑水下入臨晉。永樂，次畿。武德元年置，本隸芮州，州廢，隸鼎州，貞觀八年來屬，後又隸虢州，神龍元年復故。有雷首山。安邑，次畿。義寧元年以安邑、虞鄉、夏置安邑郡。武德元年曰虞州，又析置桐鄉縣。三年析安邑置興樂縣。貞觀元年省。十七年州廢，省桐鄉入聞喜，以安邑、解來屬。至德二載更安邑曰虞邑，乾元元年隸陝州，大曆四年復故名，元和三年來屬。有龍池宮，開元八年置。有鹽池，與解為兩池，大曆十二年生乳鹽，賜名寶應靈慶池。有銀監。寶鼎，次畿。本汾陰。義寧元年以汾陰、龍門置汾陰郡，武德元年曰泰州，州廢來屬。開元十年獲寶鼎，更名。有后土祠。襄陵，緊。本隸晉州，元和十四年隸絳州，大和元年來屬。稷山，上。

translations.literal: It had thirty-three military establishments, called Xingle, Deyi, Hubi, Longting, Qingyuan, Yonghe, Taocheng, Huoshan, Fenshui, Shouyang, Shougui, Guiren, Changqu, Yucheng, Tongrun, Baoding, Yanhai, Guichun, Dayang, Yong'an, Fengxin, Yongxing, Youwei, Fenyin, Ganquan, Pingchuan, Anbao, Shimen, Suihua, Tandao, Anyi, Chongyi, and the Six Armies. It also had Yaode Army, established in Qianyuan year two and abolished in Guangde year two. Hedong was second-rank metropolitan. It had the Fangyun Office, which drew water from the river for brewing; it was established in Wude year three and abolished in Zhenguan year ten. To the south was Fengling Pass, established in Shengli year one. It had Li Mountain. Hexi was second-rank metropolitan. In Kaiyuan year eight it was divided from Hedong and established, but was soon abolished. In Qianyuan year three, Chaoyi of Tongzhou was renamed Hexi and came under this prefecture. In Dali year five it was returned to Tongzhou, and Chaoyi and Hedong were divided off to establish it separately. It had Pujin Pass, also called Puban. In Kaiyuan year twelve eight oxen were cast, each ox having a man driving it; beneath the oxen were mountains, all of iron, set on both banks to hold the floating bridge. In year fifteen the River Temple was moved here from Chaoyi. Linjin was second-rank metropolitan. It was originally Sangquan; in Wude year three Wenquan County was divided off and established, and in year nine it was abolished. In Tianbao year thirteen its name was changed. Xie was second-rank metropolitan. It was originally Yuxiang; in Wude year one its name was changed. In Zhenguan year seventeen it was abolished and its territory entered Yuxiang; in year twenty-two it was restored. It had the Salt Pond, and also the Women's Salt Pond. It had the Ziquan Office, established in Qianyuan year one, and had twelve copper caves. Yishi was second-rank metropolitan and had Gu Mountain. Yuxiang was second-rank metropolitan. It was separately established in Wude year one. In Zhenguan year twenty-two it was abolished and its territory entered Xie; in Tianshou year two it was restored. Fifteen li north was the Sushui Canal, opened in Zhenguan year seventeen by the prefect Xue Wanche, who led the Sushui from Wenxi down into Linjin. Yongle was second-rank metropolitan. It was established in Wude year one and originally belonged to Ruizhou; when that province was abolished, it belonged to Dingzhou; in Zhenguan year eight it came under this prefecture; later it again belonged to Guozhou, and in Shenlong year one it was restored to its former status. It had Leishou Mountain. Anyi was second-rank metropolitan. In Yining year one, Anyi, Yuxiang, and Xia formed Anyi Commandery. In Wude year one it was called Yuzhou, and Tongxiang County was also divided off and established. In year three Xingle County was divided from Anyi and established. In Zhenguan year one it was abolished. In year seventeen the province was abolished, Tongxiang was abolished into Wenxi, and Anyi and Xie came under this prefecture. In Zhide year two, Anyi was changed to Yuyi; in Qianyuan year one it belonged to Shaanzhou; in Dali year four its former name was restored; and in Yuanhe year three it came under this prefecture. It had Longchi Palace, established in Kaiyuan year eight. It had salt ponds, which together with Xie's formed the two ponds; in Dali year twelve milk-salt appeared there, and they were given the name Baoying Lingqing Pond. It had a silver office. Baoding was second-rank metropolitan. It was originally Fenyin. In Yining year one, Fenyin and Longmen formed Fenyin Commandery; in Wude year one it was called Taizhou; when the province was abolished, it came under this prefecture. In Kaiyuan year ten a precious tripod was obtained, so the name was changed. It had the Shrine of Houtu. Xiangling was close-ranked. It originally belonged to Jinzhou; in Yuanhe year fourteen it belonged to Jiangzhou, and in Dahe year one it came under this prefecture. Jishan was upper-ranked.

sentences.zh: 河東，河西，臨晉，解，猗氏，次畿，有孤山。

translations.literal: Hedong, Hexi, Linjin, Xie, Yishi, secondary metropolitan vicinity, with Gushan.
translations.idiomatic: Its counties included Hedong, Hexi, Linjin, Xie, and Yishi (secondary metropolitan vicinity), the last having Gushan.

sentences.zh: 虞鄉，永樂，安邑，寶鼎，襄陵，稷山，上。

translations.literal: Yuxiang, Yongle, Anyi, Baoding, Xiangling, Jishan, upper.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxiang, Yongle, Anyi, Baoding, Xiangling, and Jishan were upper-ranked.

translations.literal: Originally subordinate to Jiang Prefecture; in the late Tang it was attached here.
translations.idiomatic: It had originally been subordinate to Jiang Prefecture and was transferred here in the late Tang.

translations.literal: There is Jishan.
translations.idiomatic: It contains Mount Ji.

sentences.zh: 萬泉，上。本隸泰州，武德三年析稷山、安邑、猗氏、汾陰、龍門置，州廢隸絳州，大順二年來屬。有介山。龍門。次畿。武德二年徙泰州來治，五年析置萬春縣。貞觀十七年州廢，省萬春入龍門，隸絳州。元和初來屬。有龍門關。有高祖廟，貞觀中置。北三十里有瓜谷山堰，貞觀十年築。東南二十三里有十石壚渠，二十三年，縣令長孫恕鑿，溉田良沃，畝收十石。西二十一里有馬鞌塢渠，亦恕所鑿。有龍門倉，開元二年置。晉州平陽郡，望。

translations.literal: Wanquan was upper-ranked. It originally belonged to Taizhou. In Wude year three, territory from Jishan, Anyi, Yishi, Fenyin, and Longmen was divided off to establish it. When the province was abolished it belonged to Jiangzhou, and in Dashun year two it came under this prefecture. It had Jie Mountain. Longmen was second-rank metropolitan. In Wude year two Taizhou was moved to govern there, and in year five Wanchun County was divided off and established. In Zhenguan year seventeen the province was abolished, Wanchun was abolished into Longmen, and it belonged to Jiangzhou. At the beginning of Yuanhe it came under this prefecture. It had Longmen Pass. It had the Temple of Gaozu, established during Zhenguan. Thirty li north was Guagushan Weir, built in Zhenguan year ten. Twenty-three li southeast was Shishilu Canal; in year twenty-three the county magistrate Zhangsun Shu dug it, irrigating good fertile fields that yielded ten shi per mu. Twenty-one li west was Ma'anwu Canal, also dug by Shu. It had Longmen Granary, established in Kaiyuan year two. Jinzhou, Pingyang Commandery, was eminent.

translations.idiomatic: Jin Prefecture (Pingyang Commandery designation), distinguished rank.

translations.literal: Formerly Linfen Commandery; renamed in the second year of Yining.
translations.idiomatic: It was formerly Linfen Commandery and was renamed in the second year of Yining.

translations.idiomatic: Its local tribute included candles; it had a Pingyang Bureau alum monopoly.

sentences.zh: 戶六萬四千八百三十六，口四十二萬九千二百二十一。

translations.literal: Households: 64,836; persons: 429,221.
translations.idiomatic: It had 64,836 households and a population of 429,221.

translations.literal: Eight counties.
translations.idiomatic: It administered eight counties.

sentences.zh: 平棘，上。東二里有廣潤陂，引太白渠以注之，東南二十里有畢泓，皆永徽五年令弓志元開，以畜洩水利。寧晉，緊。本癭陶，天寶元年更名。地旱鹵。西南有新渠，上元中，令程處默引洨水入城以溉田，經十餘里，地用豐潤，民食乃甘。昭慶，望。本大陸，武德四年曰象城，天寶元年更名。西南二十里有建初陵、啟運陵，二陵共塋。城下有灃水渠，儀鳳三年，令李玄開，以溉田通漕。柏鄉，上。

translations.literal: Pingji was upper-ranked. Two li east was Guangrun Marsh, which drew Taibai Canal to pour into it; twenty li southeast was Bihong. Both were opened by the magistrate Gong Zhiyuan in Yonghui year five to store and release water. Ningjin was close-ranked. It was originally Yingtao; in Tianbao year one its name was changed. The land was dry and saline. Southwest was New Canal; during Shangyuan the magistrate Cheng Chumo led Xiao water into the city to irrigate fields, running more than ten li, and the land became rich and moist, so the people's food became sweet. Zhaoqing was eminent. It was originally Dalu; in Wude year four it was called Xiangcheng, and in Tianbao year one its name was changed. Twenty li southwest were Jianchu Mausoleum and Qiyun Mausoleum, the two mausoleums sharing one cemetery. Below the city was Fengshui Canal; in Yifeng year three the magistrate Li Xuan opened it to irrigate fields and connect transport. Baixiang was upper-ranked.

sentences.zh: 龍岡，上。武德元年析龍岡、內丘置青山縣，開成五年省入焉。沙河，上。武德元年置溫州，四年州廢，來屬。有鐵。南和，緊。武德元年置和州，四年州廢，來屬。鉅鹿，上。武德元年置起州，幷析置白起縣。四年州廢，省白起，以鉅鹿隸趙州。貞觀元年來屬。有大陸澤。有鹹泉，煮而成鹽。平鄉，上。武德元年置封州，四年州廢，來屬。貞元中，刺史元誼徙漳水，自州東二十里出，至鉅鹿北十里入故河。任，中。武德四年置。堯山，上。本柏仁。武德元年置東龍州，四年州廢，隸趙州，五年來屬。天寶元年更名。內丘。上。武德四年隸趙州，五年來屬。有鐵。洺州廣平郡，望。

translations.literal: Longgang was upper-ranked. In Wude year one Qingshan County was divided from Longgang and Neiqiu and established; in Kaicheng year five it was abolished into Longgang. Shahe was upper-ranked. In Wude year one Wenzhou was established; in year four the province was abolished and it came under this prefecture. It had iron. Nanhe was close-ranked. In Wude year one Hezhou was established; in year four the province was abolished and it came under this prefecture. Julu was upper-ranked. In Wude year one Qizhou was established, and Baiqi County was also divided off and established. In year four the province was abolished, Baiqi was abolished, and Julu belonged to Zhaozhou. In Zhenguan year one it came under this prefecture. It had Dalu Marsh. It had salty springs, boiled to make salt. Pingxiang was upper-ranked. In Wude year one Fengzhou was established; in year four the province was abolished and it came under this prefecture. translations.literal: Linfen was eminent. Ten li northeast was Gaoliang Weir, which during Wude drew Gaoliang water to irrigate fields and entered Baijin Marsh. In Zhenguan year thirteen it was destroyed by water. In Qianfeng year two the weir collapsed, so Jin water was led from the west. It had Gushe Mountain. Hongdong was eminent. It was originally Yang, and in Yining year two its name was changed. It was originally Fushan; in Wude year two it was divided from Xiangling and established. To the southeast it had Yangjiao Mountain. In year four its name was changed because of the Shrine of Laozi. Yueyang was middle-ranked.

Thirty-five li southeast was Sha Canal; in Yifeng year two an edict ordered water from Zhongtiao Mountain to be drawn below the southern slope, flowing west for sixteen li to irrigate fields south of the Su. Yuan was upper-ranked. In Yining year one, Yuan and Wangwu formed Shaoyuan Commandery, and Qinglian and Bocheng counties were also established. In Wude year one it was called Shaozhou. In Longshuo year two it belonged to Luozhou, in Chang'an year two its former status was restored; in Zhenyuan year three it belonged to Shaanzhou, and in Yuanhe year three its former status was restored. Cizhou, Wencheng Commandery, was lower-ranked.

sentences.zh: 西南有橫海軍，開元十四年置，天寶後廢，大曆元年復置。清池，緊。西北五十五里有永濟隄二，永徽二年築。西四十五里有明溝河隄二，西五十里有李彪淀東隄及徒駭河西隄，皆三年築。西四十里有衡漳隄二，顯慶元年築。西北六十里有衡漳東隄，開元十年築。東南二十里有渠，注毛氏河，東南七十里有渠，注漳，並引浮水，皆刺史姜師度開。西南五十七里有無棣河，東南十五里有陽通河，皆開元十六年開。南十五里有浮河隄、陽通河隄，又南三十里有永濟北隄，亦是年築。有甘井二，十年，令毛某母老，苦水鹹無以養，縣舍穿地，泉湧而甘，民謂之毛公井。有鹽。鹽山，緊。武德四年置東鹽州，五年，以景州之清池幷析鹽山置浮水縣以隸之。貞觀元年州廢，省浮水，以清池、鹽山來屬。有鹽。長蘆，上。本隸瀛州。武德四年，以長蘆、平舒、魯城及滄州之清池置景州。貞觀元年州廢，以平舒還隸瀛州，長蘆、魯城來屬。樂陵，上。本隸棣州，武德八年來屬，大和二年又隸棣州，尋復來屬。饒安，上。武德四年析置鬲津縣，貞觀元年省入樂陵。無棣，上。貞觀元年省入陽信，八年復置，大和二年隸棣州，尋來屬。有無棣溝通海，隋末廢，永徽元年，刺史薛大鼎開。乾符。上。本魯城，乾符元年生野稻水穀二千餘頃，燕、魏飢民就食之，因更名。景州，上。

translations.literal: Southwest was Henghai Army, established in Kaiyuan year fourteen, abolished after Tianbao, and restored in Dali year one. Qingchi was close-ranked. Fifty-five li northwest were two Yongji dikes, built in Yonghui year two. Forty-five li west were two Minggou River dikes, and fifty li west were the eastern dike of Libiao Marsh and the western dike of the Tuhai River, all built in year three. Forty li west were two Hengzhang dikes, built in Xianqing year one. Sixty li northwest was the eastern dike of the Hengzhang, built in Kaiyuan year ten. Twenty li southeast was a canal pouring into the Maoshi River, and seventy li southeast was a canal pouring into the Zhang; both drew Fu water and were opened by the prefect Jiang Shidu. Fifty-seven li southwest was the Wudi River, and fifteen li southeast was the Yangtong River, both opened in Kaiyuan year sixteen. Fifteen li south were the Fu River Dike and the Yangtong River Dike, and thirty li farther south was the northern dike of Yongji, also built that year. It had two sweet wells; in year ten, because the magistrate Mao's mother was elderly and the bitter, salty water gave him no way to support her, the ground at the county office was dug, and a spring gushed out sweet; the people called it Lord Mao's Well. It had salt. Yanshan was close-ranked. In Wude year four Eastern Yanzhou was established. In year five, Qingchi of Jingzhou was combined with territory divided from Yanshan to establish Fushui County, which belonged to it. In Zhenguan year one the province was abolished, Fushui was abolished, and Qingchi and Yanshan came under this prefecture. It had salt. Changlu was upper-ranked. It originally belonged to Yingzhou. In Wude year four, Jingzhou was established from Changlu, Pingshu, Lucheng, and Qingchi of Cangzhou. In Zhenguan year one the province was abolished; Pingshu returned to Yingzhou, and Changlu and Lucheng came under this prefecture. Leling was upper-ranked. It originally belonged to Dizhou; in Wude year eight it came under this prefecture, in Dahe year two it again belonged to Dizhou, and soon again came under this prefecture. Rao'an was upper-ranked. In Wude year four Gejin County was divided off and established; in Zhenguan year one it was abolished into Leling. Wudi was upper-ranked. In Zhenguan year one it was abolished into Yangxin, in year eight it was restored, in Dahe year two it belonged to Dizhou, and soon came under this prefecture. It had Wudi Canal connecting to the sea; it was abandoned at the end of Sui, and in Yonghui year one the prefect Xue Dading opened it. Qianfu was upper-ranked. It was originally Lucheng. In Qianfu year one wild rice grew in more than two thousand qing of water-grain fields, and famine refugees from Yan and Wei went there to eat, so its name was changed. Jingzhou was upper-ranked.

In the mountains thirteen li south there was copper. Yicheng was eminent. In Yining year one, Yicheng and Jiang formed Yicheng Commandery, and Xiaoxiang County was also established. In Wude year one it was called Huizhou; in year two it was called Northern Huizhou; in year four the province was abolished and all the counties came under this prefecture; in year nine Xiaoxiang was abolished into Yicheng. translations.literal: It had Heyang Army, established in Jianzhong year four. Heyang was eminent. In Wude year four, Heyang, Jicheng, and Wen of Huaizhou were divided off at Heyang Palace to establish Mengzhou. In year eight the province was abolished, Jicheng was abolished into Heyang, and Wen belonged to Huaizhou. In Xianqing year two it belonged to Luozhou. It had Heyang Pass. It had the old city of Huiluo. It had a pond; in Yonghui year four Ji River water was led in to fill it, and during Kaiyuan it was used to raise yellow fish. Sishui was eminent. It originally belonged to Zhengzhou. In Wude year four Chenggao County was divided off and established; in Zhenguan year one it was abolished; in Xianqing year two it belonged to Luozhou; in Chuigong year four it was called Guangwu; and in Shenlong year one its former name was restored. It had Hulao Pass. To the southeast was the old Chenggao Pass. To the southwest was the old Xuanmen Pass. It had Niukou Isle. One li west, on Fugui Mountain, was Zhaowu Temple, established in Huichang year five. Heyin was eminent. In Kaiyuan year twenty-two it was divided from Sishui, Yingze, and Wuzhi and established; it belonged to Henan Prefecture and governed Heyin Granary, and in Huichang year three it came under this prefecture. It had Duke Liang's Weir, between the Yellow River and the Bian; in Kaiyuan year two Li Jie, governor of Henan, dredged it along an old canal to facilitate water transport. Wen was eminent. In Wude year four the Sui magistrate Zhou Zhongyin brought the county away from Wang Shichong and surrendered; Pingzhou was established, and the county town was named Li City. That year the province was abolished and it belonged to Huaizhou. In Xianqing year two it belonged to Luozhou. Jiyuan was eminent. In Wude year two Wang Shichong's general Ding Bode surrendered with the county; Western Jizhou was established, and Xiuyang, Zhengchuan, and Shaoyuan counties were also divided off and established. In year four the province was abolished, Xiuyang, Zhengchuan, and Shaoyuan were abolished, and Jiyuan belonged to Huaizhou. In Zhenguan year one Zhi County of Huaizhou was abolished into it. In Xianqing year two it belonged to Luozhou. It had Fangkou Weir; in Dahe year five the military governor Wen Zao dredged an old canal, irrigating five thousand qing of fields in Jiyuan, Henei, Wen, and Wuzhi. It had the Shrine of Jidu and the Shrine of Beihai. To the west was the old Zhi Pass. Huaizhou, Henei Commandery, was strong.

sentences.zh: 有府二，曰漁陽、臨渠。南二百里有靜塞軍，本障塞軍，開元十九年更名。又有雄武軍，故廣漢川也。東北九十里有洪水守捉，又東北三十里有鹽城守捉，又東北渡灤河有古盧龍鎮，又有斗陘鎮。自古盧龍北經九荊嶺、受米城、張洪隘度石嶺至奚王帳六百里。又東北行傍吐護真河五百里至奚、契丹衙帳。又北百里至室韋帳。漁陽，中。神龍元年隸營州，開元四年還隸幽州。有平虜渠傍海穿漕，以避海難，又其北漲水為溝，以拒契丹，皆神龍中滄州刺史姜師度開。三河，中。開元四年析潞置。北十二里有渠河塘。西北六十里有孤山陂，溉田三千頃。玉田。中。本無終，武德二年置，貞觀元年省，乾封二年復置，萬歲通天元年更名，神龍元年隸營州，開元四年還隸幽州，八年隸營州，十一年又隸幽州。有壕門、米亭、三谷、礓石、方公、白楊等七戍。營州柳城郡，上都督府。

translations.literal: It had two military establishments, called Yuyang and Linqu. Two hundred li south was Jingsai Army, originally Zhangsai Army; in Kaiyuan year nineteen its name was changed. It also had Xiongwu Army, the old Guanghanchuan. Ninety li northeast was Hongshui Garrison, thirty li farther northeast was Yancheng Garrison, and farther northeast across the Luan River was old Lulong Fortified Town, as well as Douxing Fortified Town. From old Lulong north through Jiujing Ridge, Shoumi City, and Zhanghong Pass, crossing Shiling, to the tent of the Xi king was six hundred li. Traveling farther northeast along Tuhuzhen River for five hundred li reached the administrative tents of the Xi and Khitan. Another one hundred li north reached the Shiwei tents. Yuyang was middle-ranked. In Shenlong year one it belonged to Yingzhou, and in Kaiyuan year four it was returned to Youzhou. It had Pinglu Canal, which cut a transport route alongside the sea to avoid the dangers of the sea, and north of it the swollen water formed a ditch to resist the Khitan; both were opened during Shenlong by Jiang Shidu, prefect of Cangzhou. Sanhe was middle-ranked. In Kaiyuan year four it was divided from Lu and established. Twelve li north was Quhe Pond. Sixty li northwest was Gushan Embankment, irrigating three thousand qing of fields. Yutian was middle-ranked. It was originally Wuzhong; it was established in Wude year two, abolished in Zhenguan year one, restored in Qianfeng year two, renamed in Wansui Tongtian year one, belonged to Yingzhou in Shenlong year one, returned to Youzhou in Kaiyuan year four, belonged to Yingzhou in year eight, and again belonged to Youzhou in year eleven. It had seven garrisons, including Haomen, Miting, Sangu, Jiangshi, Fanggong, and Baiyang. Yingzhou, Liucheng Commandery, was an upper-ranked area command.

Weizhou, Wei Commandery, was a grand commandery governor's office and was strong.

sentences.zh: 總章元年，李勣平高麗國，得城百七十六，分其地為都督府九，州四十二，縣一百，置安東都護府於平壤城以統之，用其酋渠為都督、刺史、縣令。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zongzhang, Li Ji subdued Goguryeo, taking one hundred seventy-six cities; the territory was divided into nine area commands, forty-two prefectures, and one hundred counties; the Andong Protectorate was established at Pyongyang to govern them, using their tribal chiefs as area commanders, prefects, and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zongzhang, Li Ji subdued Goguryeo, taking one hundred seventy-six cities; the territory was divided into nine area commands, forty-two prefectures, and one hundred counties; the Andong Protectorate was established at Pyongyang to govern them, appointing their tribal chiefs as area commanders, prefects, and magistrates.

sentences.zh: 上元三年徙遼東郡故城，儀鳳二年又徙新城。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shangyuan it was moved to the old Liaodong Commandery city; in the second year of Yifeng it was moved again to Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shangyuan it was moved to the old Liaodong Commandery city; in the second year of Yifeng it was moved again to Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 聖曆元年更名安東都督府，神龍元年復故名。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shengli it was renamed the Andong Area Command; in the first year of Shenlong it was restored to the former name.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shengli it was renamed the Andong Area Command; in the first year of Shenlong it was restored to the former name.

sentences.zh: 開元二年徙于平州，天寶二年|743年又徙于遼西故郡城。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyuan it was moved to Ping Prefecture; in the second year of Tianbao (743) it was moved again to the old Liaoxi commandery city.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaiyuan it was moved to Ping Prefecture; in the second year of Tianbao (743) it was moved again to the old Liaoxi commandery city.

translations.literal: Abolished after the Zhide era.
translations.idiomatic: It was abolished after the Zhide era.

translations.literal: Local tribute: ginseng.
translations.idiomatic: Its local tribute included ginseng.

sentences.zh: 有安東守捉。有懷遠軍，天寶二載743年置。又有保定軍。

translations.literal: It had Andong Garrison. It had Huaiyuan Army, established in Tianbao year two, 743. It also had Baoding Army.
translations.idiomatic: It had Andong Garrison. It had Huaiyuan Army, established in Tianbao year two, 743. It also had Baoding Army.

translations.literal: At right: the Hebei Surveillance Commissioner, seated at Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At right: the Hebei Surveillance Commissioner, with his seat at Wei Prefecture.
